title: Feature request: Add ability to import/configure system connections via configuration file or import command
body:
# Feature request: Add ability to import/configure system connections via configuration file or import command

## Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?

Feature Request

## Description

Administrators may want to preconfigure remote Podman system connections for users, particularly in enterprise environments where developers connect to shared development servers. Currently, administrators must either:
1. Run `podman system connection add` on each user's machine
2. Have users manually configure connections themselves

This creates friction in managed deployment scenarios.

## Background

This feature request originated from a Podman Desktop managed configuration discussion ([podman-desktop/podman-desktop#19486](https://github.com/podman-desktop/podman-desktop/issues/19486), [podman-desktop/podman-desktop#19945](https://github.com/podman-desktop/podman-desktop/pull/19945)). After technical review, the Podman Desktop team concluded that this functionality belongs in the Podman CLI rather than the desktop application, as it relates to core connection management that should be consistent between CLI and Desktop usage.

## Use Case

Administrators deploying Podman to multiple workstations (e.g., via MDM or configuration management tools) want to:
- Preconfigure remote SSH connections to shared development servers
- Ensure consistent connection configuration across teams
- Avoid requiring end-users to manually set up SSH connections

**Example scenario**: A company has 1,000 developer workstations that need to connect to a shared build server. Currently, there's no declarative way to deploy this configuration.

## Proposed Solution

Add support for one or both of the following:

### Option 1: Import command (similar to Docker contexts)
```bash
podman system connection import <connection-name> <config-file>
podman system connection export <connection-name> [<output-file>]
```

Similar to Docker's context management:
- `docker context create`
- `docker context export`
- `docker context import`

### Option 2: Enhanced configuration file support
Extend `$HOME/.config/containers/podman-connections.json` to support a system-wide or declarative configuration that can be deployed via configuration management tools.

## Required Connection Parameters

Based on the existing `podman system connection add` command, the import/configuration should support:

- **name**: Connection name
- **identity**: Path to SSH private key (e.g., `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`)
- **user**: SSH username
- **host**: Hostname or IP address (with optional port, e.g., `example.com:2222`)
- **socket**: Socket path on remote host (e.g., `/run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock` for rootless, `/run/podman/podman.sock` for root)

## Example Configuration Format

```json
{
  "name": "shared-build-server",
  "identity": "~/.ssh/id_ed25519",
  "user": "developer",
  "host": "build.example.com",
  "socket": "/run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock"
}
```

This would be equivalent to:
```bash
podman system connection add shared-build-server \
  --identity ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 \
  ssh://developer@build.example.com/run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock
```

## Benefits

1. **Simplified deployment**: Administrators can deploy connection configurations alongside Podman installation
2. **Consistency**: Same connection management approach works for both CLI and Podman Desktop
3. **Compatibility**: Aligns with similar patterns in Docker (`docker context import`)
4. **Maintainability**: Easier to version control and audit connection configurations

comments.body:
I don't see the point of import/export much given adding the same connection is just one podman system connection add command away? Like the user would have needed to create the connection at one point so they could just safe that instead of running an export to then run import on each system?

> Extend $HOME/.config/containers/podman-connections.json to support a system-wide or declarative configuration that can be deployed via configuration management tools.

Well the point of the file is that we only have our own managed connections via the cli there so that file should stay as is as that was the orginal design when we split connections out of containers.conf.

What you are looking here for is in fact already supported as part of containers.conf for basically since we added connection support. Connections can be added in a read only fashion as a drop in file ideally. So the company can have a file like `~/.config/containers/containers.conf.d/50-company-connections.conf` with this content:
```
[engine]
[engine.service_destinations]
[engine.service_destinations.production]
uri="ssh://user@production.example.com/run/user/1001/podman/podman.sock"
identity = "/some/path/to/ssh_key"

[engine.service_destinations.dev]
uri="ssh://user@dev.example.com/run/user/1001/podman/podman.sock"
identity = "/some/path/to/ssh_key"
```

Then `podman system connection ls` shows you something like this:
```
Name                         URI                                                                 Identity                                                       Default     ReadWrite
dev                          ssh://user@dev.example.com/run/user/1001/podman/podman.sock         /some/path/to/ssh_key                                          false       false
podman-machine-default       ssh://core@127.0.0.1:44509/run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock         /home/pholzing/.local/share/containers/podman/machine/machine  true        true
podman-machine-default-root  ssh://root@127.0.0.1:44509/run/podman/podman.sock                   /home/pholzing/.local/share/containers/podman/machine/machine  false       true
production                   ssh://user@production.example.com/run/user/1001/podman/podman.sock  /some/path/to/ssh_key                                          false       false
```

Notice the ReadWrite column which actually tells you where the connecting is defined, containers.conf show up as false while the ones from $HOME/.config/containers/podman-connections.json show up as true. And then `podman system connection remove` will not actually remove the connections that are read only in containers.conf.

So IMO this already works and config management system should simply distribute the containers.conf drop in files to the users.

The drop in file behavior is documented as part of containers.conf parsing and means they can even split connections across several files to be able to distribute subsets to certain machines even without having to edit the file contents when deploying the files.


So in total I would say this can be closed as already works.

---

Also for the future it would be nice if you could use our feature template from this repo please, i.e. https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/new?template=feature_request.yaml
